questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your fingers over the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces reaction time, especially in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. Riders on three-wheel motorcycles should travel one behind the other in a single-file line.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which item does NOT need adjustment?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how the motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, mirrors, and headlight. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: What is the right footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in any laces so they don't catch on anything.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply the brake.
Release the brake and only use the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: In ideal conditions, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind other vehicles?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, how should you look?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use sudden pressure on the front brake to prevent locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel and apply gentle pressure to the rear brake.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on a motorcycle after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as close to the front as possible without blocking the driver's control. Hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Fatigue while riding can be increased by:

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress to protect yourself from bad weather like wind and rain. Limit riding to about six hours per day. Stop for a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean in the right direction, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Because they are small, motorcycles may seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may seem to be traveling faster than they actually are because of their small size.

questions.question: The two main types of helmets are:
questions.explanation: The two main types of helmets are three-quarter and full-face. A full-face helmet gives the most protection.

questions.question: Which of the following helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Stay out of the center of the lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: Before riding, make sure the fuel supply valve:
questions.explanation: Before you ride, open the fuel supply valve. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines, but it will stop once those lines are empty.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so braking happens when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes are applied. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How many seconds before turning or changing lanes must you signal?
questions.explanation: Utah law requires you to signal at least two seconds before you turn or change lanes.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week as part of regular motorcycle maintenance and safety checks.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a position where oncoming drivers can see you easily. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Do not assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.
